outline: 622 Calculating the Length of the Hypotenuse
802 Calculating the Length of a Shorter Side
1307 Solving Multistep Problems with Right-Angled Triangles

examples.solution_text:
Side $a$ is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. The two shorter sides are $b$ and $c$.

$b^2+c^2=a^2$

The sum of the squares of the two shorter sides equals the square of the hypotenuse.

The hypotenuse is $m$, opposite the right angle. The student added its square to a shorter side's square; the hypotenuse must be squared on its own.

$j^2+k^2=m^2$

methods.description: Identify the side opposite the marked right angle, then equate its square to the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides. Different letters and triangle orientations use the same method.

examples.derivation: At R, vectors RS=(-2,-2) and RT=(2,-2) have dot product 0, confirming the marked right angle. Side ST, labelled a, is opposite R; b and c are the shorter sides. Therefore b^2+c^2=a^2. This follows the labelled-triangle method in lines 225–237 and image25.png.

AB is horizontal and AC is vertical, confirming the marked right angle at A. BC, labelled m, is the hypotenuse; j and k label the shorter sides. Therefore j^2+k^2=m^2. The student's equation incorrectly groups the hypotenuse's square with a shorter side's square. The correction uses the source's labelled-triangle relationship and the retained assessed correction method.
